Turn videos into a corpus carrying both what was shown and what was said

prepare_video.Rd

Turns each recording into one row, with frames in a list column and a transcript beside them. measure(text = , image = ) then reads both on the same call, since they are two columns of one row rather than two objects to align.

The audio half is prepare_audio() unchanged, running on a wav ffmpeg extracts.

Usage

prepare_video(
  x,
  ...,
  frames = 8,
  select = c("uniform", "change"),
  include_first = FALSE,
  min_gap = NULL,
  quality = 3,
  diarize_names = FALSE,
  annotate_timing = FALSE,
  tool = c("whisperx", "whispermlx"),
  asr_model = "large-v3",
  min_speakers = NULL,
  max_speakers = NULL,
  language = NULL,
  hf_token = NULL,
  extra = NULL,
  min_pause = 0.2,
  speakers = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  cache_dir = NULL,
  force = FALSE,
  verbosity = c("normal", "quiet", "verbose")
)

Arguments

x

A character vector of paths to video files, one row each. A vector rather than a directory, so list.files() is where the pattern lives.

...

Not used, and refused if anything reaches it. Every argument after it is name-only, so a misspelling lands here rather than being matched by position.

frames

An integer giving the number of frames per recording. Fixed across the corpus. Default is 8.

select

A string naming the rule that chooses the frames. "uniform" spreads them evenly and is the default. "change" takes the highest scene scores, which finds cuts and concentrates on visually busy stretches.

include_first

A logical value indicating whether the opening frame is always taken. It spends one of frames rather than adding to it, so n_frames does not vary with a flag. Frame zero has no predecessor and scores exactly zero, so change can never reach it otherwise, and an establishing shot is sometimes the most informative picture in a recording. Default is FALSE.

min_gap

A number giving the seconds below which two chosen frames may not sit. "change" only, and ignored rather than refused under "uniform", where even spacing cannot bunch. Defaults to duration / frames, which says no two frames sit closer than an even sample would put them, so "change" moves frames toward the action without being able to pack them into one stretch. Where that leaves fewer candidates than the budget, the remainder go in the middle of the widest space left.

quality

An integer giving the JPEG quality passed to ffmpeg as -q:v, 2 best to 31 worst. Default is 3.

diarize_names

A logical value indicating whether to label who is speaking. This is a transcription setting rather than a rendering one. It runs the diarizer, needs hf_token, and is in the cache key, so switching it re-transcribes. It also decides whether the text has turns in it at all, since a turn is a run of words by one speaker. Off, every silence is a [pause] and the transcript is one run of text. Default is FALSE.

annotate_timing

A logical value indicating whether silences are written into the text, as [pause 0.4s] inside a turn and [gap 0.8s] between two. Default is FALSE.

tool

A string naming the recognizer to run, "whisperx" (the default) or "whispermlx". Both emit the same JSON.

asr_model

A string naming the Whisper checkpoint, which decides the words. Both tools take the same short names. The command-line default is small, which is not the default here. Default is "large-v3".

min_speakers, max_speakers

Passed to prepare_audio() on the extracted audio, behaving there exactly as on a recording handed to it directly.

language

A string giving the spoken language, detected per file when NULL (the default).

hf_token

A string giving a HuggingFace read token, required when diarize_names is on. Default is NULL.

extra

A character vector of further flags for the recognizer, passed through verbatim and recorded on the result. Each element is its own argument, so c("--beam_size", "10") rather than one string. Default is NULL.

min_pause

A number giving the seconds below which a silence is not marked or counted. Jefferson leaves anything under 0.2 as an untimed micropause and gives a figure above it, which is where the default comes from.

speakers

A named character vector renaming the speakers, such as c(SPEAKER_00 = "Interviewer"). A name not in the timings is refused rather than ignored. Default is NULL.

id

A character vector of identifiers, one per file. Defaults to the file names without their extensions, and must be unique.

cache_dir

A string giving the directory where frames, the wav and the transcript are written and looked for. Defaults to beside each recording.

force

A logical value indicating whether to extract and transcribe again even where usable output is cached. Default is FALSE.

verbosity

A string setting how much to report.

  • "quiet" reports nothing.

  • "normal" is the default. One line per recording as it is transcribed, or in an interactive session a bar redrawn in place when there is more than one. The recognizer's own output is held rather than printed, and appears only if the call fails.

  • "verbose" lets the recognizer write to the console as it runs. These tools report their dependencies at length on every invocation, so this is for one long file rather than for a corpus.

Value

A tibble of one row per file, carrying every column prepare_audio() returns plus these.

  • video is the recording, and has_audio says whether it had a sound track at all.

  • image is a list column of frame paths in time order, which is the shape measure(image = ) takes for several pictures per document.

  • n_frames and frame_times say how many were taken and when.

  • select and include_first name which rule chose them.

  • scene_median and scene_max are the middle and largest scene score across every frame, which say whether the recording had cuts in it or whether the spacing did the work. Read before trusting "change".

Choosing frames

select = "uniform" divides the recording into frames equal segments and takes the middle of each. Midpoints rather than endpoints, since a frame at exactly zero is often a title card and one at exactly the end is often black.

select = "change" takes the frames highest scene scores instead, which ffmpeg computes for every frame as how much this picture differs from the one before it. It finds cuts that even spacing misses, and it concentrates. min_gap is what stops that, and it exists only for this mode.

Recordings without audio

ffprobe is asked whether an audio stream exists before anything is extracted. Where there is none, the row comes back with its frames and with has_audio = FALSE, text and every audio count NA, and the count is reported. A batch of campaign advertisements does not stop because three of them are silent.

exists and has_audio answer different questions and both are needed.

caseexistshas_audiotext
file not foundFALSENANA
present, silentTRUEFALSENA
present, with audioTRUETRUEthe transcript

NA on has_audio is doing work. The file was never opened, so FALSE would assert something that was not checked.

n_words is NA for a silent recording rather than 0, because nothing was transcribed. A recording whose audio track is silence is a different thing, gets transcribed, and comes back with n_words = 0.

Every other audio column is NA there too, diarized and tool and asr_model included. Nothing ran, so there is nothing to report and naming a model would assert settings that produced no words.

Frame storage

On disk beside the recording, in <stem>_frames/, because measure(image = ) reads paths.

The wav lands beside it, which is what lets prepare_audio()'s cache work unchanged. The frames keep a record of their own, <stem>_frames.fathom.json in the frames directory, holding the times they were cut at and the JPEG quality. Changing frames, select, include_first, min_gap or quality changes that record, so every frame is cut again and the old pictures are removed, while the transcript is read back from its own cache.

See also

prepare_audio(), which transcribes the sound track, and measure(), which reads both columns.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Needs ffmpeg, a recognizer and an Ollama server, so it is not run here.

ads <- list.files("campaign_ads", "[.]mp4$", full.names = TRUE)
ins <- instrument(c(attack = "Does this advertisement attack an opponent?"))

# Frames spread evenly, and whatever was said alongside them.
d <- prepare_video(ads, frames = 8)
measure(
  d,
  backend = ollama_backend("gemma3:27b"),
  instrument = ins,
  text = "text",
  image = "image"
)

# More frames, chosen where the picture moved, with the speakers labeled.
d <- prepare_video(
  ads,
  frames = 16,
  select = "change",
  diarize_names = TRUE,
  annotate_timing = TRUE,
  hf_token = Sys.getenv("HF_TOKEN")
)
} # }
